title: Maridebart cafraglutide Versus Semaglutide in Participants with Type 2 Diabetes
official: A Phase 3, Randomized, Open-Label Trial Comparing the Efficacy and Safety of Maridebart Cafraglutide Once Monthly versus Semaglutide once weekly as Add-on Therapy to Metformin With or Without a Sodium-glucose Cotransporter-2 Inhibitor in Participants with Type 2 Diabetes
summary: Main objective: To determine whether maridebart cafraglutide 00 mg Q4W is non inferior to semaglutide 00 mg QW for improvement in glycemic control in participants with T2DM treated with metformin, with or without a SGLT-2 inhibitor
conditions: T2DM inadequately controlled with metformin, with or without a sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT-2) inhibitor
criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1. Age ≥ 18 years or ≥ legal age within the country if it is older than 18 years at the time of signing informed consent.
2. Diagnosis of T2D based on the World Health Organization classification.
3. Treatment of T2D with metformin (≥ 1500 mg/day, or maximum tolerated dose as per investigator judgment) with or without an SGLT-2 inhibitor on a stable total daily dose for at least 90 days prior to randomization.
4. BMI ≥ 25 kg/m2 at screening.
5. Participants of childbearing potential must use protocol-specified contraception, during treatment and for an additional 0 weeks after the last dose of maridebart cafraglutide or an additional 0 weeks after the last dose of semaglutide or until the scheduled SFU/EOS visit (whichever is longer).
Exclusion criteria:
1. Type 1 diabetes mellitus (T1DM), history of ketoacidosis or hyperosmolar state/coma, or any other type of diabetes mellitus except T2D or past history of gestational diabetes.
2. History of chronic pancreatitis.
3. History of acute pancreatitis within 180 days before screening.
4. History of any of the following CV events within 60 days before screening: MI, CABG surgery or other major Cardiovascular surgery, stroke, or hospitalization for unstable angina, heart failure (HF), or transient ischemic attack (TIA).
5. NYHA Class IV HF
6. Use within 90 days before randomization of: Any glucose-lowering medication, except for metformin, and SGLT-2 inhibitors. Short-term (≤ 14 days) use of short-acting insulin for acute conditions, such as acute illness, hospitalization, or elective surgery is not exclusionary Medications, supplements, or alternative remedies for weight loss (e.g., GLP-1 RA, GLP-1/GIP co-agonists, phentermine, phentermine/topiramate, naltrexone/bupropion, orlistat, and sympathomimetic drugs) Chronic (> 14 days) systemic glucocorticoid therapy Excluding topical, intraocular, intranasal, intra-articular, or inhaled preparations Initiation or change in dose within 90 days before randomization or planned change in dose during trial of medications that may cause significant weight gain, including but not limited to tricyclic antidepressants, atypical antipsychotics, and mood stabilizers.
7. Thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH) < 0.4 mIU/L, or TSH > 6.0 mIU/L with free thyroxine below the lower limit of normal at screening. Participants who receive treatment for hypothyroidism are permitted in the trial, if their thyroid hormone replacement dose has been stable for at least 90 days before randomization and their TSH at screening is not exclusionary.
8. eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m2 according to the 2021 CKD-EPI or receiving dialysis at screening.
9. Acute or chronic hepatitis, signs and/or symptoms of any liver disease other than metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease, or ALT level > 3.0 x ULN, or TBL > 1.2 x ULN.
10. Currently pregnant or breastfeeding, or planning to become pregnant or breastfeed while on trial until an additional 0 weeks after the last dose of trial intervention.
11. Participants who are currently receiving or planning to receive treatment for diabetic retinopathy and/or macular edema (e.g., laser photocoagulation or intravitreal injections of anti-vascular endothelial growth factor inhibitors).
12. Participants who have a diagnosis of proliferative diabetic retinopathy, diabetic maculopathy, or severe non-proliferative diabetic retinopathy.
13. One or more episode of severe hypoglycemia (Level 3 hypoglycemia) within 180 days before screening, as defined by the occurrence of neuroglycopenic symptoms requiring the assistance of another person for recovery.
14. History of hypoglycemia unawareness or poor recognition of hypoglycemic symptoms.
15. Self-reported change in body weight > 5% within 90 days before screening. Participant must also agree to not initiate an intensive diet or exercise program during the trial with the intent of reducing body weight, other than the lifestyle and/or dietary measures for diabetes treatment.
16. Previous or planned (during the trial) surgical, endoscopic, or device-based treatment for obesity.
17. Participant has known sensitivity or intolerance to any of the products or components to be administered during dosing.
18. History of malignancy within the last 5 years before screening (except for the following treated with curative intent: nonmelanoma skin cancer, breast ductal carcinoma in situ, or cervical carcinoma in situ).
